title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Earlier in the manuscript, Gl(2,Z)^~ (resp. Sl(2,Z)^~) is the group of lifts to the universal cover R of the circle S_0 (directions in the plane, identified with the unit circle U) of the action of Gl(2,Z) (resp. Sl(2,Z)). It is a central extension of Sl(2,Z)/±1 by Z = <ω_0>, where ω_0 is a generator of the deck group (essentially a half-turn lift). Lifts ρ~ and σ~ of the elliptic generators ρ (order 6) and σ (order 4) are normalised by the 'characteristic conditions' (20), which express ρ~^3 and σ~^2 as powers of ω_0. In the image these read ρ~^3 = ω_0^{-1} and σ~^2 = ω_0.

In §1 on the previous page, the reflection τ, and the more convenient τ' (swap of e_0 = 1 and e_1 = i), is lifted to an involution of R: t ↦ 1/2 − t, resp. t ↦ 1/8 − t. This page continues with that lift.

Step 1: the involution acts on the centre. Conjugation by τ~ (or τ~') acts on ω_0 by inversion, ω_0 ↦ ω_0^{-1}. This is because it reverses the orientation of the circle.

Step 2: formula (24). Claim: τ~'(ρ~) = ρ~^{-1} and τ~'(σ~) = σ~^{-1}.
- These hold mod the centre, i.e. downstairs in Gl(2,Z), where τ'ρτ' = ρ^{-1} and τ'στ' = σ^{-1}.
- So upstairs the two sides differ by a power ω_0^k.
- Since Z is torsion-free, k is pinned down by checking that the left-hand sides satisfy the normalisation (20).
- That check reduces to τ~'(ω_0) = ω_0^{-1}, which holds by Step 1. OK.

Theorem (25). Sl(2,Z)^~ has the one-relator presentation <ρ~, σ~ | ρ~^3 σ~^2 = 1>. Up to replacing ρ~ by its inverse, this is <x, y | x^3 = y^2>.

Proof (begun here, finished on the next page). Let Π be the group defined by this presentation. Map it to Sl(2,Z)/±1 = <ρ, σ | ρ^3 = σ^2 = 1>. The kernel is the normal closure of ω_0 = ρ~^3, which is central, so the kernel is the cyclic group <ω_0>. Compare the resulting sequence Z → Π → PSL(2,Z) → 1 with the exact sequence 1 → Z → Sl(2,Z)^~ → PSL(2,Z) → 1 and apply the five lemma. Hence Π ≅ Sl(2,Z)^~.

Corollary (next page). Gl(2,Z)^~ = Sl(2,Z)^~ ⋊ Z/2, where the involution τ~' inverts both generators.

In modern terms: Sl(2,Z)^~ is the preimage of PSL(2,Z) in the universal cover of PSL(2,R). This is the trefoil knot group, isomorphic to the braid group B_3 and to the universal central extension of PSL(2,Z). Gl(2,Z)^~ is its extension by an orientation-reversing involution. The purpose, within the Longue Marche, is to have explicit presentations of the genus-1 Teichmüller-type groups, with their orientation-reversing extensions, for the Galois-theoretic study of the 'tour de Teichmüller'.
errors: Sign/normalisation inconsistency. On this page the underbraces give ρ~^{-3} = ω_0 and σ~^{-2} = ω_0^{-1}, so ρ~^3 = ω_0^{-1} and σ~^2 = ω_0; the boxed relation reads ρ~^3·σ~^2 = 1. The next page writes ω_0 = ρ~^3 = σ~^2. The two conventions differ by replacing ρ~ with ρ~^{-1}, so this is harmless for the group but inconsistent as written.

The phrase 'valables dans Sl(2,Z)' should strictly mean valid modulo the central subgroup <ω_0> (i.e. in PSL(2,Z) or Gl(2,Z)). The lifting argument is nonetheless correct, because Z is torsion-free: an element x ≡ ρ~^{-1} mod <ω_0> satisfying the normalisation x^{-3} = ρ~^3 is unique.
Minor: the five-lemma comparison needs Z → Π to be injective. This follows a posteriori, since its composite with Π → Sl(2,Z)^~ is injective; the argument as written handles this implicitly.

ideas.what: Preimage of SL(2,Z) in the universal cover of the circle-action group is a central Z-extension of PSL(2,Z) with presentation <x, y | x^3 = y^2>
ideas.modern_name: Universal central extension of PSL(2,Z) ≅ braid group B_3 ≅ trefoil knot group ≅ preimage of PSL(2,Z) in the universal cover of PSL(2,R)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Artin; Milnor, Introduction to Algebraic K-theory; Serre, Trees)
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (genus-1 Teichmüller groups); not stated in this form as far as I know

ideas.what: Lifting an orientation-reversing involution and checking it inverts the canonical lifts ρ~, σ~ using torsion-freeness of the centre
ideas.modern_name: Semidirect product B_3 ⋊ Z/2 (extended mapping class group of the once-punctured torus / its universal cover version)

ideas.what: Five-lemma proof of the presentation via central extension of PSL(2,Z) = Z/2 * Z/3
ideas.modern_name: Presentation of central extensions of amalgamated products

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but entirely classical computation: the presentation <ρ~, σ~ | ρ~^3 = σ~^2> of the universal-cover lift of SL(2,Z), i.e. B_3, and its Z/2-extension by an orientation-reversing involution. Interesting only as documentation of Grothendieck's working out of the genus-1 Teichmüller groups in the Longue Marche.
transcription_corrections: 'τ~^1' throughout should be read as τ~' (tau-prime, the lift of τ' = [[0,1],[1,0]]).
Boxed relation (25) reads 'ρ~^3 · σ~^2 = 1', not 'ρ~^3 = σ~^2'. This is consistent with the underbraces ρ~^{-3} = ω_0 and σ~^{-2} = ω_0^{-1}.
Underbrace under ρ~^{-3} is ω_0 (with a mark), not ω_0^{-1}. The equation line reads τ~'(ρ~^{-3}) = ω_0^{-1} and τ~'(σ~^{-2}) = ω_0.
'elles sont valables mod dans Sl(2,Z)' should read 'elles sont valables dans Sl(2,Z)' (Sl appears to be written with a doubled/overwritten letter).
In (26), the right-hand side carries the additional annotation '= {ρ, σ | ρ^3 = σ^2 = 1}', and the map is (ρ~, σ~) ↦ (ρ, σ) mod {±1}.
